elements.label: Figure 7.5: The impact of fiscal policy on inequality by fiscal instrument
elements.description: Waterfall-style column chart. Y-axis: "Percentage Point Reduction", ticks 0.0 to 6.0 in steps of 1.0. Categories left to right, with approximate floating bar ranges (values not printed, so readings are approximate): Cash transfer (~0.0 to ~0.4); PIT (~0.5 to ~1.0); Other direct taxes (~1.0 to ~1.2); SSC/HI (~1.2 to ~2.7); After direct and indirect taxes and transfers (consumable) (~0.0 to ~2.7, dark teal total bar); Electricity subsidy (~2.7 to ~2.9); VAT (~2.8 to ~2.9); Excise (~2.8 to ~2.9); Environmental tax (~2.7 to ~2.8); After direct and indirect taxes (~0.0 to ~2.8, gold total bar); Education (~2.7 to ~4.4); Health (~4.1 to ~5.0); After all taxes and transfers (final income) (~0.0 to ~5.0, orange total bar). Note: marginal effects on poverty reduction are shown; a positive bar is a contribution to poverty reduction and a negative bar an increase in poverty; subcomponents are scaled to the marginal effect of each fiscal category (VAT, excises and environmental taxes sum to the indirect taxes marginal effect). Source: 2018 VHLSS and World Bank calculations. Visible pattern: the cumulative bars step up from near zero to about 5.0 points, with the largest increments from SSC/HI, education and health, and the subtotals for consumable and final income marking the totals.
